newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 96,500 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 44.787 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 49,500 tonnes, in Denmark 20,000, in the U.K. 12,000, in the Netherlands 6,000, in Belgium 5,500, in Germany 3,000 and in Finland 500 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.516 million tonnes. This compares with the 7,500 tonnes awarded on February 14, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.596 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-July to be 44.787 Ecus per 100 kilos, the exact amout awarded.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 40,000 and 90,000 tonnes versus 22,750 last week when the restitution was 45.519 Ecus.
